scenes.tts: If the cortex kept the bulb's map, where would one glomerulus send its output?
scenes.visual: Title card: Following One Glomerulus. One gold glomerulus with a question mark over a blank cortex rectangle.
scenes.narration: If the cortex kept the bulb's map, where would one glomerulus send its output?

scenes.tts: A topographic map keeps neighbours together. Then one glomerulus should land in one patch of cortex.
scenes.visual: A neat topographic projection: a row of inputs maps onto matching patches. A dashed patch appears on the cortex rectangle.
scenes.narration: A topographic map keeps neighbours together. Then one glomerulus should land in one patch of cortex.

scenes.tts: Sosulski and colleagues asked whether the wiring does that. They put a tracer into a single glomerulus of an adult mouse.
scenes.visual: A pipette delivers tracer into one gold glomerulus in a row. Label: Sosulski and colleagues, 2011.
scenes.narration: Sosulski and colleagues asked whether the wiring does that. They put a tracer into a single glomerulus of an adult mouse.

scenes.tts: Five days later, they imaged where the labelled axons went.
scenes.visual: A box reads: five days.
scenes.narration: Five days later, they imaged where the labelled axons went.

scenes.tts: They looked in two targets: piriform cortex and, for comparison, the cortical amygdala.
scenes.visual: Two blank tissue rectangles side by side, labelled piriform cortex and cortical amygdala.
scenes.narration: They looked in two targets: piriform cortex and, for comparison, the cortical amygdala.

scenes.tts: Pause and predict. In piriform cortex, will the axons gather in a patch or spread out? Must both targets agree?
scenes.visual: On screen: Patches or scatter? Do both targets follow one rule? The rectangles stay blank.
scenes.narration: Pause and predict. In piriform cortex, will the axons gather in a patch or spread out? Must both targets agree?

scenes.visual: the question stays on screen

scenes.tts: In piriform cortex the axons spread diffusely, with no apparent spatial preference.
scenes.visual: Gold labelled axons fill the piriform rectangle evenly, with no patch.
scenes.narration: In piriform cortex the axons spread diffusely, with no apparent spatial preference.

scenes.tts: In the cortical amygdala, the same glomerulus gave stereotyped patches.
scenes.visual: Gold axons gather into separate patches in the cortical amygdala rectangle.
scenes.narration: In the cortical amygdala, the same glomerulus gave stereotyped patches.

scenes.tts: One tracer in one glomerulus showed two different rules in two different targets.
scenes.visual: The two rectangles side by side, one diffuse, one patchy. Label: one glomerulus, two rules.
scenes.narration: One tracer in one glomerulus showed two different rules in two different targets.

scenes.tts: It would have been easy to conclude that the bulb projects at random everywhere. The cortical amygdala shows it does not.
scenes.visual: The two rectangles side by side, one diffuse, one patchy. Caption: different targets, different projection rules.
scenes.narration: It would have been easy to conclude that the bulb projects at random everywhere. The cortical amygdala shows it does not.

scenes.tts: So the scatter is not a property of the whole bulb. It was seen in piriform cortex, not in the amygdala.
scenes.visual: Label over the two rectangles: scatter in piriform cortex, patches in the amygdala.
scenes.narration: So the scatter is not a property of the whole bulb. It was seen in piriform cortex, not in the amygdala.

scenes.tts: A tracer image shows where axons go. It does not show which synapses each neuron makes.
scenes.visual: A small card: axons are not synapses.
scenes.narration: A tracer image shows where axons go. It does not show which synapses each neuron makes.

scenes.tts: Recordings of responses tell the same story. Stettler and Axel imaged odour responses in piriform cortex of living mice.
scenes.visual: An imaging field of piriform cortex. Label: Stettler and Axel, 2009, in vivo.
scenes.narration: Recordings of responses tell the same story. Stettler and Axel imaged odour responses in piriform cortex of living mice.

scenes.tts: An odour activated a dispersed ensemble. Its neurons were scattered across the area, not gathered in a patch.
scenes.visual: One odour puff; responsive cells light up scattered across the field.
scenes.narration: An odour activated a dispersed ensemble. Its neurons were scattered across the area, not gathered in a patch.

scenes.tts: A neuron's receptive field is the set of odours that excite it.
scenes.visual: One cell circled. Beside it, a list of odours with ticks for those that excite it. Label: receptive field.
scenes.narration: A neuron's receptive field is the set of odours that excite it.

scenes.tts: A single piriform neuron could respond to chemically dissimilar odours.
scenes.visual: The ticked odours are drawn as clearly different structures.
scenes.narration: A single piriform neuron could respond to chemically dissimilar odours.

scenes.tts: Its receptive field was discontinuous in chemical space.
scenes.visual: A chemical-space plot; the cell's odours are isolated points far apart, not a single region.
scenes.narration: Its receptive field was discontinuous in chemical space.

scenes.tts: This does not say piriform carries no chemical information. It says the arrangement is not a topographic map.
scenes.visual: Two labels: no spatial map (tick). No chemical information? (question mark, left open).
scenes.narration: This does not say piriform carries no chemical information. It says the arrangement is not a topographic map.

scenes.tts: Diffuse is also not the same as random.
scenes.visual: The diffuse axon picture with the word random crossed out.
scenes.narration: Diffuse is also not the same as random.

scenes.tts: Later projection mapping found spatial structure in how bulb neurons route their axons. It was not a map of odour chemistry.
scenes.visual: Bulb neurons route axons to matched targets; label: structure in routing, not a map of chemistry.
scenes.narration: Later projection mapping found spatial structure in how bulb neurons route their axons. It was not a map of odour chemistry.

scenes.tts: So the scatter is real, and it belongs to piriform cortex. Next comes the harder question: how can a scatter keep chemistry?
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: Piriform input is diffuse; the cortical amygdala gets patches. How can a scatter keep chemistry?
scenes.narration: So the scatter is real, and it belongs to piriform cortex. Next comes the harder question: how can a scatter keep chemistry?
